title: ELECS Refresher — Exam Solving
subject: Electronics Engineering Problem Solving
description: Problem-solving reviewer from the uploaded ELECS refresher exam, with an Apple Pencil/iPad solution pad. Source-inconsistent items are preserved but not graded.

questions.solution: Use R = ρL/A. Convert ρ = 1.7 μΩ·cm = 1.7×10⁻⁸ Ω·m and A = 0.077 cm² = 7.7×10⁻⁶ m². R ≈ (1.7×10⁻⁸)(36.6)/(7.7×10⁻⁶) = 0.0808 Ω → D. The other choices are powers-of-ten errors.

Source/options issue. If reverse saturation current doubles for every 10°C rise, a 25°C rise gives a factor 2^(2.5)=5.657. The final current is 565.7% of the original, while the strict percentage increase is 465.7%. Choice C matches 'percent of original,' not the wording 'percentage increase,' so this card is not graded.
Terminal voltage while delivering current is V = E − Ir = 2.2 − (1)(0.03) = 2.17 V → A. A value above the emf would violate the discharging-cell relation.
Use the mass-action law np = nᵢ². Minority concentration = (1.5×10¹⁶)²/(5×10²⁰) = 4.5×10¹¹ m⁻³ → A. The other values do not satisfy np=nᵢ².
Temperature coefficient = [(10.2−10)/(10(100−25))]×100 = 0.0267 %/°C → B. The alternatives come from omitting either the original voltage or the 75°C interval.

Source/options issue. Using the printed values C=4425 pF, A=80 cm² and εr=2.5 gives d=ε₀εrA/C≈0.040 mm, which is not among the choices. If the intended capacitance were 442.5 pF, the answer would be 0.40 mm (A). This card is intentionally not graded.
For transistor leakage, ICEO=(β+1)ICBO. Thus β = ICEO/ICBO − 1 = 0.4 mA/5 μA − 1 = 79 → D. The base-current value is not needed for this relation.
Twelve identical cells in series add emf and internal resistance: E=12(1.5)=18 V and r=12(0.24)=2.88 Ω → A.

Source/options issue. The printed leakage-current/temperature data do not uniquely produce any listed barrier voltage without an additional diode-model assumption (such as ideality factor or room-temperature forward voltage). The card is left ungraded rather than forcing an unsupported option.
Electric flux density D=εE, so E=D/(ε₀εr)=2×10⁻⁶/[8.854×10⁻¹²(5)]≈45.2 kV/m → A.
For series-aiding coupled coils, L=L1+L2+2M and M=k√(L1L2). With k=1: L≈44+88+2√(44·88)=256 mH≈260 mH → D.
For an abrupt-junction varactor, C≈C0/√(1+VR/VJ)=60 pF/√(1+3/0.6)≈24.5 pF. Xc=1/(2πfC)≈1.30 kΩ → A.
Area=0.20×0.40=0.08 m². Electric flux density D=Q/A=0.2 μC/0.08=2.5 μC/m². Electric field E=V/d=250/0.005=50 kV/m → A.

For a Ge diode at 27°C, I/Iₛ≈e^(V/VT)−1. With V=0.06 V and VT≈25.9 mV, the forward-current magnitude is about 9–10 times the reverse saturation current; the listed value 9.45 is the intended result → C.
P=VI, so V=P/I=10 W/10 A=1 V → C. The other values do not satisfy the power relation.

Source/options issue. The printed 'E MOSFET' data VGS=−4 V, ID=8 mA and VGS=+6 V, ID=32 mA do not give any listed k under the usual square-law enhancement-MOSFET model. The source itself circles C, but the printed data are inconsistent, so this card is not graded.
Source/options issue. Using the Shockley diode equation with the printed Is=10⁻¹⁸ A, η=1.05, I=70 μA at room temperature gives about 0.86 V, which does not match the choices. This card is not graded.
Enhancement MOSFET square law: ID=k(VGS−VGS(th))²=0.001(5.5−2.5)²=0.009 A=9 mA → B.
36 MJ in 1 h corresponds to P=36×10⁶/3600=10 kW. At 250 V, I=P/V=10000/250=40 A → B.
Using the practical silicon model V≈0.7 V + IrB: I=(0.9−0.7)/0.5=0.4 A=400 mA → A. The lower-current choices use a larger assumed junction drop.
For a diffused/graded varactor junction, C=C0/(1+VR/VJ)^(1/3). C=80/[1+4.2/0.7]^(1/3)=80/7^(1/3)≈41.82 pF → C.

Source/options issue. β increases from 100 to 200. α1=100/101=0.990099 and α2=200/201=0.995025. The relative increase is about 0.4975%, while the absolute change is about 0.4926 percentage point; no listed option matches exactly. Not graded.

Source/options issue. With 75 mm × 75 mm plates, d=0.2 mm and εr=5, C=ε0εrA/d≈1.25 nF, but all printed choices are roughly 22–34 nF. The printed data and choices do not agree, so this card is not graded.
Force on a current-carrying conductor: F=BIL sinθ. With B=0.9 T, I=20 A, L=0.30 m: at 90°, F=5.4 N; at 30°, F=2.7 N → A.

Source/options issue. At the depletion/enhancement transition VGS=0. Using the clearly visible gate divider gives about VG=1 V; combining that with the printed IDSS value does not cleanly match the listed RS choices. The source circles A, but the card is left ungraded because the scan/data are ambiguous.
The magnetic circuit has two series reluctances. Using l1=6 cm, A1=1 cm², l2=2 cm, A2=0.5 cm² and μr=750 gives flux ≈7.54×10⁻⁵ Wb, so B in the smaller 0.5 cm² section ≈1.51 T → A.
Circular-mil area of one strand is d(mils)². Radius=0.2 in gives diameter=0.4 in=400 mils. One strand=160,000 CM; 12 strands=1,920,000 CM → A.
Motional emf e=Blv=1.25(0.300)(4)=1.5 V. Load current=1.5/20=0.075 A=75 mA → A.

Source/options issue. Using the printed C=0.2 μF, V=1.25 kV, dielectric strength=50 MV/m, safety factor=2 and εr=6 gives a required thickness about 0.05 mm and area about 1880 cm². No printed pair matches, so this card is not graded.
Reluctance ℜ=l/(μ0μrA)=0.150/[4π×10⁻⁷(4000)(1800×10⁻⁶)]≈1.658×10⁴ H⁻¹. Absolute permeability μ=μ0μr≈5.027×10⁻³ H/m → A.
R∝ρL/A. Manganin has 30× the resistivity, 1/3 the length, and 1/3 the diameter, so area is 1/9. Ratio=30(1/3)/(1/9)=90. Thus R=90 Ω → D.
For an ideal diode, current ratio I2/I1=e^(ΔV/VT). ΔV=VT ln9≈25.9 mV(2.197)≈56.9 mV; the closest listed value is 59.6 mV → C.
Motional emf e=Blv. v=e/(Bl)=9/[0.6(0.075)]=200 m/s → A.
Faraday's law: e=−NΔΦ/Δt=−200(25 mWb)/(50 ms)=−100 V → A. The minus sign is Lenz's-law polarity.
RD=(20−12)/2.5 mA=3.2 kΩ. For the JFET, ID=IDSS(1−VGS/VP)² gives VGS≈−1.06 V. With gate grounded, VS≈+1.06 V and RS≈1.06/2.5 mA≈425 Ω≈400 Ω → C.
From the β=150 operating point: RC=(6−3)/1.5 mA=2 kΩ and IB=1.5 mA/150=10 μA. The fixed-bias base current remains about 10 μA when β=200, so IC≈2 mA and VCE=6−(2 mA)(2 kΩ)=2 V → A.
For a transformer-coupled Class-A stage, efficiency scales as 50%(Vpeak/VCC)² for a symmetric sinusoidal output relative to the maximum swing. With Vpeak/VCC=6/12=0.5, η≈50%(0.5)²=12.5% → A.
For a Ge diode at 300 K, V≈VT ln(I/Is)=25.9 mV·ln(50 mA/5 μA)=25.9 mV·ln(10⁴)≈0.238 V → C.
